source.description: Where the certificate comes from, from the certificate registry. Null where the installation has no registry or no entry names this certificate.

targets.description: Which clusters and receivers the certificate is published to, from the certificate registry. Null where source is null.

published_copy.description: Whether one target holds this certificate, and since when. published_at is when the manager last wrote the file and says nothing about whether anything fetched it: a receiver pulls on its own schedule with its own key and reports nothing back. current is null where it could not be decided, which is a different fact from being out of date.

published_receiver.description: One receiver target and the state of its copy. Spelled out rather than composed with published_copy, because additionalProperties only sees the properties of the schema it sits in and a composed id would be rejected as unexpected.

format.description: Additive (C7, B159): the form this certificate is written in for this receiver. Absent from an older producer, where it means pem. current is null for pkcs12, which cannot be read without the password that opens it.

registered_certificate.description: One certificate the manager holds, measured at its source rather than at a target. The source is what a renewal writes first, so a target that has not been published yet would otherwise report the previous certificate.

distribution.description: The shared cluster copy under certificate_root. One fact and not one per cluster, because every cluster reads the same file; null where no cluster names this certificate. Which nodes are carrying it is a different measurement and lives in the node status.

interface.description: Additive (B188): present and true on the one entry that is the manager's own interface certificate. It has no targets and is published to nginx.

exportable.description: Additive (B255): present and true on an entry to be taken out and installed by hand. It has no targets; its key may be exported through the export helper and is never reported here.

fullchain_pem.description: Additive (B255): the certificate and its chain, PEM, for an exportable entry whose material could be read - public by construction, so the interface can offer it for download. Absent otherwise.

request_state.description: Additive (C6): an import whose material has not arrived because an NDES enrollment for it is still waiting on the CA, or (C9b) because a signing request made on the manager is waiting for its signature. Absent otherwise.

request.description: Additive (C9b): the signing request a pending row is waiting on, when it was made on the manager. The CSR is public by construction; the key it was made for waits in the import store and is never reported. Absent for an NDES request and for every row with material.

renewal.description: Additive (2026-09-15): what the scheduled NDES renewal last did to this certificate. Absent where it has not tried.

measured_at.description: Where the facts were read: the certificate's own source, or the published cluster copy when the source holds nothing yet - an import registered before the import helper exists. Null when nothing could be read.

registry.description: Every certificate the registry names, regardless of cluster, plus the registered receivers that may be chosen as targets. Absent where the installation declares no certificate_registry. Carried in this per-cluster answer rather than by a helper of its own, because the poller is indexed by cluster in every one of its cache tables.

manager.description: The name a receiver reaches this manager by - the interface's server name - for the fetch commands the receivers page writes out (B142). Null where the helper could not read it.

interface_served.description: Additive (B188): what nginx serves the manager's interface with now, read from the configured pair - the registry's marked certificate once installed, the installer's self-signed pair before. Null where the helper could not read it.

receiver_records.description: One record per registered receiver, for the interface's receivers page (B142): how it fetches and which certificates name it. `flat` is the layout of a receiver registered before C7.
